prompt: The client wants to know why profit fell from 2023 to 2025.
flawed_answer: Revenue grew 10% from 2023 to 2025, reaching $220M.
right_parts: it reads the chart correctly and backs the point with a figure from it
model_repair: Cost of goods sold grew 25%, from $120M to $150M, while revenue grew only 10%, so gross profit fell from $80M to $70M.

prompt: The client wants to know why its company-wide on-time delivery rate fell this year.
flawed_answer: Both regions slipped from March and kept falling, so the decline is company-wide.
right_parts: it dates the start of the decline to March
model_repair: Nearly all the decline is in the South: from March its on-time rate slid from 93% to 78% by June, while the North held near 95%.

prompt: The client's sales are falling, and it wants to know why.
flawed_answer: The main competitor's advertising is pulling customers away, while the client held its price at $10.
right_parts: it notes that the client held its price at $10
model_repair: The main competitor cut its price 20%, from $10 to $8, while the client held at $10, so the client is likely losing sales on price.

prompt: The client wants to speed up truck unloading across its warehouses.
flawed_answer: Warehouse C unloads trucks about as fast as the others, at around 40 minutes.
right_parts: it singles out warehouse C, and gives the other warehouses' time correctly (around 40 minutes)
model_repair: Warehouse C takes 85 minutes to unload a truck, about twice the 38 to 42 minutes at the others, so C is where to speed things up.

prompt: The client wants to know whether its new snack is a lasting success.
flawed_answer: Sales more than doubled from week 1 to week 3, reaching 220k units.
right_parts: it reads the week 3 peak correctly (220k units)
model_repair: Sales peaked at 220k units in week 3 and have halved since, to 110k in week 6, so the snack doesn't look like a lasting success yet.

prompt: The client wants to know why its cost per unit rose.
flawed_answer: Materials added $6 per unit, the biggest increase, but material prices will fall next year, so the rise will reverse.
right_parts: it names materials as the largest increase, $6 per unit
model_repair: Materials drove most of the rise: they added $6 of the $11 in increases that took cost per unit from $50 to $57, net of $4 saved by automation.

prompt: The client can fund one project and requires payback within 3 years.
flawed_answer: Project A is the one to fund: it throws off the most cash, $3M a year, and its size makes it the safest bet.
right_parts: it backs the point with a figure read correctly from the table
model_repair: Fund Project C: it is the only one that pays back within 3 years ($6M ÷ $2M a year), against 4 years for B and 5 for A.

prompt: The client wants to know why its cost per delivery rose.
flawed_answer: All three cost components rose from 2023 to 2025, because a shortage of drivers pushed up costs across the board.
right_parts: it explains the rise through the cost components
model_repair: Driver pay explains the whole $3 rise in cost per delivery: it went from $5 to $8, while fuel's $1 rise and vehicle costs' $1 fall cancel out.

prompt: The client is choosing which region to enter first.
flawed_answer: The West is the region to enter: it is the biggest market, at $88M in 2025.
right_parts: it reads the chart correctly and backs the point with a figure from it
model_repair: Enter the South first: its market grew 75% in three years, from $40M to $70M, against about 10% for the West and the North, though the West is bigger today at $88M.

prompt: The client tested four prices for a subscription and wants the one that maximizes revenue.
flawed_answer: $10 is the best price: it loses only 8% of subscribers compared with $8, so it earns the most.
right_parts: it reads subscribers at $10 correctly (92k)
model_repair: $12 maximizes revenue: 80k × $12 = $960k, against 92k × $10 = $920k and 100k × $8 = $800k.

prompt: The client's costs are rising and it wants to know where to look first.
flawed_answer: Labor is where to look: it is the largest cost, at $54M in 2025.
right_parts: it reads the chart correctly and backs the point with a figure from it
model_repair: Look at materials first: they rose $18M, from $30M to $48M, most of the $22M rise in total costs, while labor grew only $4M.

prompt: The client wants to acquire a target that is both growing fast and profitable.
flawed_answer: Company C is the target: it combines the most revenue, $150M, with solid growth.
right_parts: it commits to one company, as the client asked
model_repair: Company A is the target: it grows 25% a year at an 18% margin, while B grows 5% and C, the largest at $150M, only 2% at a 12% margin.

prompt: The client wants to know why profit fell from 2024 to 2025.
flawed_answer: Labor was the biggest drag on profit, costing $5M, while higher prices added $8M.
right_parts: it reads the $8M gain from price correctly
model_repair: Materials drove the fall: they cost $22M, wiping out the $8M from price and $4M from volume, so profit fell from $50M to $35M.

prompt: The client wants to enter the European country where it is easiest to win share.
flawed_answer: France is the easiest place to win share, since it has a long tail of small players.
right_parts: it judges the countries by how fragmented they are
model_repair: Spain is the easiest place to win share: it is the most fragmented, with 45% outside the top two players, against 35% in Germany and 15% in France.

prompt: A city health department wants to cut average ER waiting times across its four hospitals.
flawed_answer: Hospital C's waits are the problem because it is short of doctors and nurses.
right_parts: it singles out Hospital C
model_repair: Hospital C is where to start: its average wait is 120 minutes, more than double the 45 to 50 minutes at the other three hospitals.

prompt: The client's costs rose about 10% this year, and it wants to know where.
flawed_answer: Sales and marketing added similar amounts, since sales is the bigger budget, and the marketing increase hasn't paid off.
right_parts: it looks at sales and marketing, the two budgets that rose most
model_repair: Marketing drove most of the rise: its budget grew 40%, about $7M of the $10M increase, against about $2M for sales and under $1M for IT.

prompt: The client is choosing a launch price for a new juice, based on a survey.
flawed_answer: $9 is the price to pick: it is the highest price, so it earns the most per shopper surveyed.
right_parts: it compares the prices by what they earn per shopper
model_repair: Launch at $7: per 100 shoppers surveyed it earns $315 (45 × $7), against $300 at $5 and $180 at $9, where only 20% would buy.

prompt: The client wants to know how serious a new rival is.
flawed_answer: The rival isn't serious yet: the client's share has been stable and is still larger.
right_parts: it notes the client still has the larger share
model_repair: The rival is serious: it gained 13 points of share in three years, from 10% to 23%, while the client lost 9, from 40% to 31%, though the client is still larger.

prompt: The client's lenders want to know why its cash balance is falling.
flawed_answer: Cash is falling because dividends were the largest outflow, at $10M.
right_parts: it reads the dividend outflow correctly ($10M)
model_repair: Cash is falling because outflows of $50M (capex $25M, interest $15M, dividends $10M) exceed the $30M of operating cash, a net outflow of $20M.

prompt: The client wants to know which plan matters most for its revenue.
flawed_answer: Basic, with the most customers, earns the most revenue, and its customers are the most satisfied.
right_parts: it reads Basic as the plan with the most customers
model_repair: Plus matters most: 28,000 customers at $25 bring in $700k a month, ahead of $600k from Basic, which has the most customers, and $200k from Pro.

prompt: The client wants to know where to invest for growth.
flawed_answer: Both channels contributed to growth, online the most, so the client should invest in both.
right_parts: it identifies online as the biggest source of growth
model_repair: Invest in online: it rose $43M, from $20M to $63M, and drove all the growth, while store revenue fell $8M, from $80M to $72M.

prompt: The client is deciding whether to build a third plant.
flawed_answer: Both plants are near full capacity, so the client needs a third plant.
right_parts: it reads Plant A as near full
model_repair: The client may not need a third plant: Plant A runs at 98%, but Plant B is at only 63%, with about 37 points of spare capacity.

prompt: The client wants to know which store is dragging down chain profit.
flawed_answer: Store 3 loses money mainly because its rent is so high, and its lease is up for renewal soon.
right_parts: it singles out Store 3, which loses $150k
model_repair: Store 3 is the drag, losing $150k: its revenue is about $290k below the other stores' average ($600k against about $890k), a bigger gap than its rent, about $140k above theirs.

prompt: The client wants to pick a city for its first pet grooming salons.
flawed_answer: Boston is the city to pick: it is the largest market, at $80M.
right_parts: it reads the chart correctly and backs the point with a figure from it
model_repair: Austin is the city to pick: a $50M market growing 12% a year with a leader at only 20%, while Boston is bigger at $80M but grows 3% and has a 55% leader.

prompt: The state wants to know why its overall graduation rate fell.
flawed_answer: Every district's graduation rate fell, with District C falling the most.
right_parts: it singles out District C as the biggest fall
model_repair: Only District C fell, by 14 points, from 78% to 64%, while Districts A and B each rose a point, so C explains the state's drop.

prompt: The board asks where the deal's value comes from.
flawed_answer: Procurement makes up 60% of the synergies, and those savings will be easy to achieve.
right_parts: it says procurement makes up 60% of the synergies
model_repair: Procurement is where the value comes from: $30M of the $50M in annual synergies, 60%, against $5M to $8M from each of the other areas.

prompt: The client wants to cut delivery time in the South.
flawed_answer: Transit is the slowest step in the South, so faster shipping is the fix.
right_parts: it looks at the South's delivery steps one by one
model_repair: The South's warehouse step is the bottleneck: it takes 5 days, against 2 in the North and West, while transit takes 2 days.

prompt: The client wants to know which products earn the weakest margins.
flawed_answer: Pastries earn the weakest margin, at 10%, because they are the best-selling product.
right_parts: it names pastries' 10% margin as the weakest
model_repair: Pastries earn the weakest margin, at 10%, far below every drink, which earn 30% to 60%.

prompt: The client is deciding which segment of the market to enter.
flawed_answer: Budget is the segment to enter: it is over twice the size of premium.
right_parts: it reads the chart correctly and backs the point with a figure from it
model_repair: Enter premium: it grew 75% in three years, from $20B to $35B, while budget shrank from $80B to $75B, though budget is still twice the size.

prompt: Customers are switching to a rival, and the client wants to know why.
flawed_answer: The client trails the rival on speed and on service, so both need fixing.
right_parts: it names speed as a gap
model_repair: Speed is why: the rival scores 9 to the client's 5, the widest gap, while price is tied and the client leads on selection and service.

prompt: The client wants to know which channel is driving the growth in new customers.
flawed_answer: Referral grew faster than social, so referral is driving the growth.
right_parts: it compares the channels by how much they grew
model_repair: Social drives the growth: it added 10k new customers, from 25k to 35k, of the 12k total added, while search added 2k and referral 1k.

prompt: A call center wants to cut waiting times without hiring.
flawed_answer: Waits build steadily through the day, so the center needs more agents all day.
right_parts: it reads the chart correctly and backs the point with a figure from it
model_repair: Waits spike only at midday, reaching 12 to 14 minutes at 12pm and 1pm, and stay at 6 minutes or less the rest of the day, so moving agents to midday is the lever.

prompt: The city wants to raise its overall recycling rate.
flawed_answer: East recycles only 15% because it lacks recycling bins.
right_parts: it singles out East's 15% rate
model_repair: East is where to focus: it recycles 15%, about a third of the 42% to 45% in the other neighborhoods.

prompt: The client is valuing an acquisition target.
flawed_answer: EBITDA grew, since revenue rose faster than margins fell, and the target is cutting prices to grow.
right_parts: it weighs revenue growth against falling margins
model_repair: EBITDA shrank from $10M (50 × 20%) to about $7M (86 × 8%) as margins fell faster than revenue grew, despite 72% revenue growth.

prompt: The client wants to move marketing budget to the channel that brings in the most revenue per dollar spent.
flawed_answer: Search is the channel to fund: it brings in the most revenue, $12M, and its customers are the most loyal.
right_parts: it reads search's revenue correctly ($12M)
model_repair: Move budget to social: it returns about $8 of revenue per dollar ($8M on $1M), twice search's $4 ($12M on $3M) and four times TV's $2.

prompt: A warehouse club asks whether its revenue is growing.
flawed_answer: Revenue grew, since members rose faster than spend fell, and new members are bargain hunters.
right_parts: it weighs member growth against falling spend per member
model_repair: Revenue fell about 10% despite 50% more members: 100k members at $500 brought $50M in 2022, and 150k at $300 brought $45M in 2025.

prompt: The client wants to know which region added more revenue since 2020. In 2020, North had $200M of revenue and South $50M.
flawed_answer: North added more revenue, since it is four times South's size, and South's growth came from new stores.
right_parts: it uses each region's 2020 size
model_repair: South added more: its index rose to 160, so 60% of $50M is about $30M, while North's rose to 110, 10% of $200M, or $20M.

prompt: The client wants to cut the number of customers it loses each year.
flawed_answer: The longest-tenure group loses the most customers, since it is four times larger, because long-time customers get bored.
right_parts: it works from the group sizes in the table
model_repair: First-year customers account for the most losses, about 5,500 a year (10,000 × 55%), more than the 4,800 lost from the 40,000 customers of three years or more.

prompt: The client's labor costs jumped this quarter.
flawed_answer: Overtime has tripled since week 4 because staff are leaving.
right_parts: it says overtime tripled from week 4
model_repair: Overtime explains the jump: it tripled from week 4, from about 200 hours a week to about 600.

prompt: The client keeps raising prices and asks whether it should continue.
flawed_answer: Keep raising prices: units held up well as prices rose from $10 to $13.
right_parts: it reads the price path correctly ($10 to $13)
model_repair: Stop raising prices: as price rose from $10 to $13, the last increase cut revenue from $1.08M (90k units at $12) to $0.91M (70k at $13).
